title: Context Bagging: Inference-Time Ensembling for Robust Long-Context QA Under Hard Distractors

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to allocate test-time compute to context diversity instead of decoding diversity for robust long-context QA. No prior paper explicitly addresses this objective. While papers like [5] and [6] discuss retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for question answering and multi-hop questions, they do not focus on the specific problem of reallocating test-time compute to context diversity over decoding diversity. Therefore, the purpose is **not covered**.

### Mechanism
The mechanism, Context Bagging (CoBag), involves sampling K diverse context subsets via relevance-weighted selection, randomly permuting paragraph order within each subset, generating answers with greedy decoding, and aggregating by majority voting. Papers like [2], [8], [9], [14], and [30] discuss bagging and ensemble methods, which involve sampling subsets and aggregating predictions, but none describe relevance-weighted selection combined with random permutation of paragraph order and majority voting in the context of long-context QA. While [12] and [28] discuss majority voting for self-consistency, they do not incorporate the specific combination of techniques used in CoBag. Thus, the mechanism is **not covered**.

### Evaluation
The evaluation uses a noisy MuSiQue split with hard distractors, where CoBag significantly outperforms self-consistency. Papers like [5], [6], [10], [17], and [28] evaluate RAG systems or self-consistency methods under noisy or challenging conditions, using benchmarks and metrics that assess robustness and distractor handling. The evaluation design (benchmarking under noisy conditions and comparing against self-consistency) is conceptually similar to these prior works, even though the specific dataset (MuSiQue) and instance differ. Therefore, the evaluation is **covered**.

### Domain
The domain is long-context question answering / RAG. Papers like [1], [3], [4], [5], [6], [10], and [17] all work within the general application area of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and question answering. Although the specific dataset or sub-problem (long-context QA) may differ, the domain is clearly within the established area of RAG-based QA. Therefore, the domain is **covered**.
